- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent high), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +5% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling >2% from prior high), model tends to lag → adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > -0.1), model often overestimates downward trend → reduce forecast slope downward by 1–2% per day.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window → apply 2–5% downward bias to first 5–7 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (avg > 0.1) and price is rising, model often fails to capture momentum → increase forecast by 1–3% per day for next 3–5 days.
